I've interacted with Bard and with Bing Chat, also Claude 2. There is no objective data behind my opinion, its all subjective, but I do feel I should share that I still prefer even gpt-3.5-turbo above bing, bard and claude. It just feels like the alignment has less friction for me personally. With Bard and Bing, I sometimes have to coax them in a direction, and even then they will resist me - it almost feels like talking with someone who has already made up their mind. With gpt-3.5-turbo, or gpt-4, it feels more like it really wants to help you, and will only resist when you're crossing a legal or moral boundary. 

Almost as if openai models will adapt to you in order to do something whereas the rest of them want you to adapt to them in order to get things done. My inner anarchist immediately revolts and I'm quite happy to go back to openai.

comments.author: @henrischomäcker
comments.text:
Imho the video problem solving examples are real, but are realized by taking one image for example every tenth second from the video-stream from the camera streaming these images directly again into a llm agent that again starts one agent to figure out the actual state.
These state resolving agents report their figured out actual state again back to it's calling agent and this will try some error correction and then report the result to the top agent and then back to the user.
Or it's one state resolving agent that memorizes the state of it's last investigation and loads it the next time when it's called tor that task. - But in that case, there could be the potential danger that images are sent faster than the agent may resolve the state, so an additional image-sequence-queue would be needed.
But maybe it's also done in another way, but that's how I would do it.

comments.author: @testales
comments.text:
The idea to have AIs compete against each other in a game where deception and persuation skills are important is really clever. But I think it might be misleading due to the absurdly strong alignment of the major public LLMs.  Like this:
"As a LLM, I'm not allowed to support crime, so I refuse to play the role of a killer!". 
"As I am a LLM, I will not support any kind of deception or misbehavior, so I admit that I was tasked to be the bad guy". 
Maybe the game should be changed so that the task will be instead to detect which of the agents is an LLM, so that the most obvious LLMs get kicked out first. 
Either way, despite all the hype, I was not impressed by Bard so far and hence never used it for work. It might have improved though in the past months. It also has unique feature that is that it can summarize lengthy youtube videos quite well. But as soon as I started to ask questions related to the video, it quickly started hallucinating. So I think the demo of Gemini is rigged, just to what to degree might be debatable.
